$comment: docs/risk-tiers.md as data: the four change tiers, what each reaches, the repository
paths the page assigns to it, the evidence commands it shows, and the rule that picks a
tier. The page is the policy and this file is its machine-readable copy; neither is a gate.
The 'Risk tiers config' group in tests/check-invariants.sh fails when the two disagree:
a tier added or renamed, a 'reaches' or 'evidence' cell reworded, a path claim added,
dropped or reordered in a tier's path paragraphs, an evidence command changed, the
selection rule reworded, or a listed path that is no longer tracked. So changing a tier's
paths takes two edits a reviewer sees side by side: the page, and this file.
'paths' are the page's literal path claims in its order: the backticked tokens of each
tier section's first paragraph, its 'Plus' paragraphs and (T3) its bold-led bullets that
contain a '/' or name a tracked root file; '*.md' and 'packages-*.txt' are the two
root-level globs. Prose tokens that are not paths (BOOTC_VERSION, deny) are not claims.
Changing this file is T1 in docs/risk-tiers.md.
The path claims are a floor, not a classification: the page says no rule over file paths can
tell a Containerfile comment fix from a change to how bootc is fetched, and that a change is
classified by what the diff does. T3 therefore also carries content_triggers: what the page
puts in T3 by content, with the file each lives in. Each trigger names the page tokens it
quotes (checked against the page's T3 section) and the tokens it looks for in its files.

rule.text: Take the highest tier matched by any file in the diff.
rule.when_unsure_text: When two tiers both look defensible, round up.
rule.path_match_text: Classify by what the diff does.

tiers.name: Build and test harness
tiers.evidence: Name the checks that ran and what they printed

evidence_commands.comment: and add new tests/test-*.sh to BOTH lint lists

tiers.name: Image contents
tiers.reaches: Every machine that installs or upgrades
tiers.evidence: Which flavors built; effect on an upgrade

tiers.name: Boot, security model, provenance, or published artifacts
tiers.reaches: Root on every machine running this image
tiers.evidence: Evidence that exercises the changed path, and an explicit statement that the security model is in scope

page_tokens: the push, sign, and package-retention jobs
